Actually the mapped_rxn shows product on left? Let's parse: "(CCO[C:8]([CH2:7][C@@H:6]1[O:5][C@H:4](/[CH:3]=[C:2](/[CH3:1])[C:22](OC)=[O:23])[C@H:20]([CH3:21])[C@@H:11]([O:12][Si:13]([CH3:14])([CH3:15])[C:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19])[CH2:10]1)=[O:9])>>([CH3:1]/[C:2](=[CH:3]/[C@H:4]1[O:5][C@@H:6]([CH2:7][CH:8]=[O:9])[CH2:10][C@H:11]([O:12][Si:13]([CH3:14])([CH3:15])[C:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19])[C@H:20]1[CH3:21])[CH2:22][OH:23])"

So left side is product? Actually typical retrosynthesis: product >> precursors. So left side is product (target) and right side is precursors (two fragments). The product SMILES likely corresponds to the first SMILES from earlier? Let's check: product includes CCO[C:8]... which is maybe the first SMILES? Actually CH2OH is "CO". So second fragment is "CO". But also there is maybe a third? Wait the right side shows two fragments: first is a larger molecule, second is CH2OH. So the precursors list should be two SMILES: the larger fragment and "CO". However the earlier answer from make_5_lvl1-apply_template-2 gave two SMILES: the product and another maybe? Actually that answer gave two SMILES: the product and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That second SMILES is not "CO". So maybe there are multiple possible templates?
